uncited: Radiative and Tomographic Gaussians adapt 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for X-ray imaging by replacing view-dependent color and opacity with view-independent scalar density or radiation intensity [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).

This modification solves the problem of reconstructing volumetric data from 2D attenuation measurements, where radiation depends on the integrated density along the ray path rather than surface appearance [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).

Unlike standard 3DGS, which uses spherical harmonics for view-dependent appearance, these methods remove angular dependence to model isotropic density fields [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).
The family shares the core 3DGS primitive representation but modifies the radiative transfer model to align with X-ray physics [S1].
The scene is represented by a set of $M$ 3D Gaussian kernels $\mathcal{G}_3 = \{G_i\}_{i=1}^M$ [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).

*   **Central Density ($\rho_i$):** Used in [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md) to model isotropic density fields for CT reconstruction [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).
*   **Radiation Intensity ($I_i$):** Used in [X-Gaussian](4525-x-gaussian.md) to represent direct radiation intensity [X-Gaussian](4525-x-gaussian.md).

*   **Feature Vector ($\mathbf{f}_i$):** Used in [Radiative Gaussian Point Cloud Model](5304-radiative-gaussian-point-cloud-model.md), mapped to intensity via a Radiation Intensity Response Function (RIRF) [Radiative Gaussian Point Cloud Model](5304-radiative-gaussian-point-cloud-model.md).
**Ray Space Transformation:** 3D Gaussians are transformed into ray space to align viewing rays with the coordinate axis [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).
**Projection:** 3D Gaussians are projected to the 2D image plane [S1].
In radiative models, $c_i$ is unity or related to source intensity, and attenuation is modeled via the scalar density/intensity [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).

The method originates from the adaptation of 3D Gaussian Splatting [3D Gaussian Splatting](1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) to X-ray imaging, where the physical model of light interaction (reflection/emission) is replaced by X-ray attenuation (absorption/scattering) [S1].
Standard 3DGS assumes view-dependent appearance, which is invalid for X-rays where attenuation is path-integrated and isotropic [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).

This family enables differentiable rendering of X-ray projections, allowing for gradient-based optimization of 3D density fields from 2D projections [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).
